metaData.title: The Open Agent Leaderboard
metaData.oneSentenceSummary: IBM Research and Hugging Face launch the Open Agent Leaderboard, an open benchmark that evaluates full AI agent systems (not just models) across diverse tasks, reporting both quality and cost to measure true agent generality.
metaData.summary: This article announces the Open Agent Leaderboard, a collaborative project between IBM Research and Hugging Face. It addresses a critical gap in AI evaluation: most benchmarks only score models, but deployed agents are complex systems involving planning, tool use, memory, and error recovery. The leaderboard evaluates full agent systems across six diverse benchmarks (SWE-Bench Verified, BrowseComp+, AppWorld, tau2-Bench variants) covering coding, customer service, research, and personal assistance. It introduces a unified protocol to standardize interactions across these different benchmarks. Key findings include: general-purpose agents are already competitive with specialized ones, agent architecture (beyond just the model) measurably impacts results and costs, and failed runs cost 20-54% more than successful ones. The project is fully open-source, including the Exgentic evaluation framework and a companion paper. The leaderboard aims to become a community standard for evaluating general-purpose agent systems.

mainPoints.point: The Open Agent Leaderboard evaluates full agent systems, not just the underlying models.
mainPoints.explanation: It measures how an agent's architecture (planning, tool use, memory, error recovery) combined with a model performs across diverse tasks, revealing that the same model can yield very different results depending on the agent system wrapped around it.

mainPoints.point: General-purpose agents are already competitive with specialized, benchmark-tuned systems.
mainPoints.explanation: In several benchmarks, agents without any benchmark-specific customization matched or outperformed systems built specifically for those tasks, suggesting that general agency is becoming a practical reality.

mainPoints.point: Agent architecture is a measurable driver of both performance and cost.
mainPoints.explanation: Techniques like tool shortlisting improved performance across all tested models, and the cost of failed runs (20-54% more than successes) highlights that failure behavior is a critical economic factor in production deployments.

keyQuotes: How well an AI agent works depends on how it's built, not just the model inside it.
A more general agent is one you can drop into a new setting and have it just work.
Same model, different agents, different results -- the agent matters.
Today the model explains most of the results. But the agent around it is already starting to change the outcome.
General agents are too important to be evaluated behind closed doors.

relatedArticles.title: Introducing NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Nano Omni: Long-Context Multimodal Intelligence for Documents， Audio and Video Agents
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: NVIDIA introduces Nemotron 3 Nano Omni, a new open-weight omni-modal model that combines text, image, video, and audio understanding with a hybrid Mamba-Transformer-MoE backbone, achieving top accuracy on multiple multimodal leaderboards while delivering up to 9x higher throughput.

relatedArticles.title: New in Claude Managed Agents: dreaming， outcomes， and multiagent orchestration | Claude
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Claude Managed Agents introduces dreaming for self-improving memory, outcomes for rubric-based self-correction, and multiagent orchestration for complex task delegation.

relatedArticles.title: Harness design for long-running application development
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article explores Anthropic's multi-agent harness design (Planner, Generator, Evaluator) for long-running autonomous coding, detailing how to overcome context anxiety and self-evaluation bias to build complex full-stack applications.

relatedArticles.title: Building a Fast Multilingual OCR Model with Synthetic Data
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article details NVIDIA's development of Nemotron OCR v2, a fast and accurate multilingual OCR model trained on a massive, open-source synthetic dataset of 12.2 million images, overcoming data scarcity through a scalable, language-agnostic rendering pipeline.

relatedArticles.title: How NVIDIA AI-Q Reached \#1 on DeepResearch Bench I and II
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: NVIDIA AI-Q achieves state-of-the-art performance on deep research benchmarks through a modular multi-agent architecture, fine-tuned Nemotron-3 models, and specialized reliability middleware.

relatedArticles.title: Specialization Beats Scale: A Strategic Variable Most AI Procurement Decisions Overlook
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: A 3-billion-parameter specialized model outperformed every commercial frontier API in a structured OCR benchmark at roughly fifty times lower cost, demonstrating that distributional alignment to the deployment task can be more decisive than parameter count.

relatedArticles.title: OpenAI Introduces GPT-5.5: A New Class of Intelligence for Agents
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: OpenAI announces GPT-5.5, a new model designed for complex goal understanding and autonomous task completion, now available in ChatGPT and Codex.

relatedArticles.title: State of the Claw
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: OpenClaw founder and OpenAI engineer Peter Steinberger discusses the unprecedented growth and security challenges of the OpenClaw project, shares his unique AI-assisted development workflow, and explores the evolving concept of 'engineer taste' in the AI era.

relatedArticles.title: Martin Fowler & Kent Beck: Frameworks for reinventing software， again and again
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Software legends Martin Fowler and Kent Beck discuss how AI redefines software engineering, emphasizing that core practices like TDD and modularity remain essential for human-AI collaboration.

relatedArticles.title: Falcon Perception
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Falcon Perception is a 0.6B early-fusion Transformer that unifies vision and language in a single backbone for open-vocabulary grounding and segmentation, outperforming SAM 3 on complex compositional prompts.
